risks.note: Shipping performance is closely linked to the state of the global economy; adverse global economic growth would have an unfavourable effect on the shipping market.

OPEC nations control about one-third of world oil supply and many crude-producing/exporting countries are politically volatile; the Strait of Hormuz has been effectively closed to normal traffic since the beginning of March 2026, illustrating how sanctions, wars and political change in these regions can alter the supply-demand balance and tanker markets.
Trade disputes between countries can escalate into trade wars with tariff and non-tariff barriers, which could significantly impact trade volumes and shipping routes.
China has been a major driver of global commodity demand growth; a faltering Chinese economy or a change in its import policy would cause significant consequential damage to shipping demand.

The shipping industry is exposed to a host of global supply-demand issues, resulting in significant volatility in freight earnings and asset values; the Company manages this via time charters (6 months to 3 years), freight derivatives, fleet-mix adjustments and operating across multiple asset classes/markets to avoid dependence on a single market.

The Company's business is predominantly USD-denominated (freight rates and ship values in USD, liabilities also in USD), so significant movements in currency or interest rates could meaningfully impact the Company's financials.

Indian officers are in high global demand, but unfavourable taxation on seafarers sailing on Indian-flagged vessels makes it difficult to source officers capable of meeting modern worldwide trading requirements.
Described as 'a new and worrying threat to our business'; the Company is taking steps to secure assets and systems, including protective measures and ongoing employee training.

one-line thesis: Strong global crude and offshore demand has driven TCE rates and NAV growth, but the company is withholding capital deployment due to elevated asset prices, maintaining a $500M+ net cash position while paying consistent dividends; the disconnect between high operational earnings and low investment activity defines its current strategic stance.
financial scorecard: revenue: +28% YoY (driven by crude/LPG TCE spikes); EBITDA/margin: +32% YoY, margin 58% (normalized); PAT (rptd): INR 813cr; PAT (normalized): INR 805cr (minimal FX/derivatives distortion); order book: N/A (no newbuild orders); net debt: +$500M net cash (up from $360M net debt in FY19)
guidance: revenue growth: no formal guidance; margin: expects sustained high margins if rates hold; order inflow: none expected in near term; capex/commissioning: modest fleet modernization (replacing old with newer vessels), no capacity expansion
order book & pipeline: Crude tankers: 17%; Product tankers: 19%; Dry bulk: 12.5%; LPG: 29%; jack-up rigs: extremely low (near zero new orders in last 10 years)
segment / subsidiary detail: Crude tankers: TCE up 40% YoY due to Russian trade rerouting and Brazil/Guyana export surge; Product tankers: recovered from prior weakness; Dry bulk: Capesize strength from China iron ore stockpiling; LPG: spot earnings strong despite lower volumes due to longer US-SE Asia ton-miles; Offshore: OSV utilization at 65-66% (healthy), jack-up rig utilization at 84-85% (up from 75%); Saudi Aramco recalling 9 rigs in CY2026
growth verticals / optionality: No newbuilds planned; potential for fleet modernization via replacement of older vessels; offshore segment growth tied to Saudi Aramco and Indian O&G project timelines (e.g., KG-D6, ONGC wells), but no visibility on vessel demand quantification
margins & cost dynamics: Margins sustained by high TCE rates; direct operating expenses pass-through; no material cost inflation; drydocking costs absorbed due to strong rates; no wage or fuel cost pressure cited
capex / expansion: Capex focused on fleet modernization: selling older vessels (20+ yrs) and replacing with newer second-hand assets; no newbuilding orders; December FY26 saw cash deployment for modernization; capex for FY26 estimated at INR 1,500-2,000cr
capital allocation: Dividend payout increased to ~25% of earnings (from 17-18%); net cash >$500M retained for future downturn deployment; no buybacks or M&A planned; no LNG fleet investment due to high capex ($250M/ship) and long-term contract structure
risks & watch-items: Asset price correction could erode NAV; rupee appreciation would reduce FX tailwind on cash holdings; prolonged weak freight rates could trigger scrapping but unlikely in near term; geopolitical disruption to Russian crude flows; offshore demand slowdown if O&G capex cuts occur
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic on market fundamentals; confident in high earnings sustainability; explicitly avoiding new investments due to overvalued asset prices; proud of cash position as strategic buffer; dismissive of near-term LNG opportunity; tone is defensive, patient, and capital-preservation focused
non-obvious takeaways: Despite record cash and earnings, the company is not expanding — it’s preserving capital for the next downturn, mirroring its 2018-19 strategy; the 'old fleet' (20+ yrs) is 24% of crude tankers but scrapping is minimal because rates cover drydocking costs; offshore vessel demand is decoupled from rig count due to multi-use vessels (pipelines, cables); 500+ offshore vessels in cold layup are effectively dead capacity

| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Crude tanker market tightness due to Russian trade rerouting and reduced supply | THE GE SHPG.LTD | beneficiary | High | Direct beneficiary of higher TCE rates from increased ton-miles and reduced vessel availability |
| Offshore jack-up rig utilization recovering from Saudi Aramco’s rig recall | THE GE SHPG.LTD | beneficiary | High | 9 rigs returning to service in CY2026 will boost offshore segment earnings |
| High asset prices and low order book in shipping sectors | New entrants in offshore or tanker markets | loser | Med | High cost of entry, low liquidity in second-hand market, and experience barriers deter new competitors |
| Potential rupee appreciation and reduced FX tailwind | THE GE SHPG.LTD | loser | Low | Current FX gains are a temporary tailwind; if rupee strengthens, cash returns will decline |

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: GE Shipping owns, operates and manages a fleet of tankers (crude, product and LPG carriers) and dry bulk carriers, providing international marine transport of crude oil, refined petroleum products, gas and dry bulk commodities to oil majors, refineries, manufacturers, miners and producers. As on March 31, 2026 the fleet comprised 40 vessels (26 tankers, 14 dry bulk carriers) aggregating 3.20 Mn dwt with an average age of 14.59 years, trading in Indian and international waters.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Crude tankers: TCE up 40% YoY due to Russian trade rerouting and Brazil/Guyana export surge; Product tankers: recovered from prior weakness; Dry bulk: Capesize strength from China iron ore stockpiling; LPG: spot earnings strong despite lower volumes due to longer US-SE Asia ton-miles; Offshore: OSV utilization at 65-66% (healthy), jack-up rig utilization at 84-85% (up from 75%); Saudi Aramco recalling 9 rigs in CY2026

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Tankers:** Crude oil carriers (Suezmax, Aframax), Product carriers (LR1/LR2, MR), LPG carriers (VLGC)
- **Dry Bulk:** Capesize carriers, Kamsarmax carriers, Ultramax carriers, Supramax carriers

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Crude tankers: 17%; Product tankers: 19%; Dry bulk: 12.5%; LPG: 29%; jack-up rigs: extremely low (near zero new orders in last 10 years)

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: revenue growth: no formal guidance; margin: expects sustained high margins if rates hold; order inflow: none expected in near term; capex/commissioning: modest fleet modernization (replacing old with newer vessels), no capacity expansion

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: No newbuilds planned; potential for fleet modernization via replacement of older vessels; offshore segment growth tied to Saudi Aramco and Indian O&G project timelines (e.g., KG-D6, ONGC wells), but no visibility on vessel demand quantification

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Crude tanker: robust supply-demand fundamentals, OPEC+ unwinding of voluntary production cuts (~2.5 mbpd released), new upstream supply from Brazil and Guyana, and elevated geopolitical risk premiums supported earnings through FY26
- Crude tanker: escalation of the West Asia conflict and disruption to transits through the Strait of Hormuz (constraining ~30% of global seaborne crude trade at the peak) drove earnings to unprecedented levels late in FY26
- Crude tanker: modest global fleet growth (~1% nominal) against steady demand expansion produced a constructive supply-demand balance during the year
- Crude tanker outlook: short-term outlook highly uncertain, hinging on the duration of the Middle East conflict and Strait of Hormuz transit levels; medium-term outlook supported by a gradual recovery in regional production/exports and potential stock rebuilding by importers
- Crude tanker outlook: increasing ownership concentration among large tanker operators has improved commercial discipline, supporting earnings resilience during disruptions
- Product tanker: higher newbuilding deliveries (LR2/MR) capped H1 FY26 earnings, but ~90 LR2 vessels (~15% of the global LR2 fleet) switching to dirty trades tightened effective product tanker supply and supported H2 FY26 earnings
- Product tanker: US refinery utilisation and refined product exports rose in H2 FY26 (exports +12% y/y in Jan-Feb 2026), while the West Asia conflict caused a sharp, temporary decline in Gulf product exports
- Product tanker outlook: higher oil prices and a softer macro environment may weigh on refined product demand; trade-flow and inventory adjustments by consuming regions expected to keep influencing tanker utilisation near-term
- LPG/VLGC: escalation of the US-China trade conflict materially redrew global LPG trade routes (US volumes redirected to Far East/India/SE Asia; China diversified sourcing to MEG/Canada/Australia), increasing tonne-mile demand; India LPG imports grew ~9% y/y
- LPG/VLGC outlook: short-term outlook sensitive to Strait of Hormuz transit conditions; increased US eastbound LPG movements may raise competition for Panama Canal transit slots, supporting tonne-mile demand via longer alternative routes; fleet growth expected to accelerate from FY27 with a substantial orderbook
- Dry bulk: Capesize was the best-performing segment on continued strength in iron ore and bauxite trade; coal demand faced headwinds; grain trade supported by firm Chinese soybean demand and South American exports
- Dry bulk outlook: broadly positive trade growth outlook, with Capesize tonne-miles expected to benefit from the gradual ramp-up of the Simandou iron ore project in Guinea, though a slowdown in Chinese domestic steel demand is a headwind
- Asset values: crude/product tanker asset prices rose 15-35% and dry bulk asset prices rose 15-25% in FY26 depending on vessel age/type, while VLGC second-hand values held at historically high levels
- Crude tanker orderbook increased sharply to approximately 20% of the fleet, versus 11% a year earlier
- Product tanker orderbook stood at around 19% of the fleet
- VLGC fleet growth is expected to accelerate from FY27 onwards, with a substantial orderbook scheduled for delivery over the next two years
- Bulk carrier orderbook is around 13% of the fleet, with the fleet expected to grow at approximately 3% in CY2026, consistent with CY2025 growth

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Margins sustained by high TCE rates; direct operating expenses pass-through; no material cost inflation; drydocking costs absorbed due to strong rates; no wage or fuel cost pressure cited

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Dividend payout increased to ~25% of earnings (from 17-18%); net cash >$500M retained for future downturn deployment; no buybacks or M&A planned; no LNG fleet investment due to high capex ($250M/ship) and long-term contract structure

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The routed capex_expansion text carries no company-specific fleet-addition or newbuild narrative (fleet delivery/sale details sit outside this bundle); the only capex-adjacent disclosure here is BRSR Principle 2's R&D/capex-on-environmental-improvement metric, under which the Company's capex on technologies to improve environmental and social impact was USD 6,84,483 in FY26 versus USD 34,16,629 in FY25, with prior-year detail noting that LR1 tankers were fitted with redesigned propellers and MAN B&W EcoCam retrofits were completed on select vessels during dry-docking to aid emission reduction at part-load engine operation.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Cautiously optimistic on market fundamentals; confident in high earnings sustainability; explicitly avoiding new investments due to overvalued asset prices; proud of cash position as strategic buffer; dismissive of near-term LNG opportunity; tone is defensive, patient, and capital-preservation focused

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- India's premier private-sector maritime leader with a 77-year legacy in the global shipping arena
- Blue-chip client base and deep market intelligence enabling tailored solutions to complex global demands
- Disciplined fleet renewal program that phases out older tonnage and adds younger, technologically advanced vessels, structurally lowering overall carbon intensity
- Diversified fleet across crude, product and LPG tankers plus dry bulk carriers, spreading exposure across multiple shipping sub-cycles
- Broad deployment of energy-efficiency retrofits (EGCS, Mewis Ducts, redesigned propellers, MAN B&W EcoCam, adaptive autopilot, ultrasonic biofouling protection) supporting fuel savings and regulatory compliance

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Asset price correction could erode NAV; rupee appreciation would reduce FX tailwind on cash holdings; prolonged weak freight rates could trigger scrapping but unlikely in near term; geopolitical disruption to Russian crude flows; offshore demand slowdown if O&G capex cuts occur

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Despite record cash and earnings, the company is not expanding — it’s preserving capital for the next downturn, mirroring its 2018-19 strategy; the 'old fleet' (20+ yrs) is 24% of crude tankers but scrapping is minimal because rates cover drydocking costs; offshore vessel demand is decoupled from rig count due to multi-use vessels (pipelines, cables); 500+ offshore vessels in cold layup are effectively dead capacity

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Supply / orderbook] Orderbook-to-fleet cited as 27% for crude tankers and 21% for product tankers, ~14% for dry bulk, and "elevated at 35%" for VLGC - the historical orderbook chart carries the values 27.1, 20.7, 13.9 and 34.9 for crude tankers, product tankers, bulkers and LPG carriers (65k+ cbm) respectively.
- [Geopolitics / demand] Q1 FY27 market commentary hinges on conflict: global dirty volumes fell 12% y/y as the "stand off over Hormuz continued" while Atlantic trade rose 13% y/y supporting ton-miles; ~25% of the LR2 clean fleet switched to dirty trade post the West Asian war; Middle East VLGC export volumes fell to less than one-third y/y while US exports rose 26% y/y and US LPG exports to India rose 134% y/y, with the US accounting for nearly 68% of India's imports in the quarter.
- [Offshore market] Industry data slide: current fleet 3,341 vessels and 490 rigs; fleet under contract 2,312 vessels and 330 rigs; orderbook 99 vessels and 12 rigs (3.00% and 2.4% of current fleet); 840 vessels and 152 rigs more than 20/30 years old (26% and 31% of fleet); 393 vessels and 58 rigs cold stacked more than 3 years. Footnote flags that "June 26 data includes all the rigs on contract including the rigs on put on standby due to the war in Middle East".
- [Board transition] Mr. K. M. Sheth stepped down as Chairman and Board member in Nov'25 and was appointed 'Chairman Emeritus' for life; Mr. Bharat K. Sheth was appointed Chairman & Managing Director in Nov'25, having been Deputy Chairman & Managing Director for more than 20 years, and is also Chairman of Greatship (India) Ltd.
- [Valuation reference] The deck plots Share Price to Consolidated NAV, showing 0.74 for 1Q27, with a footnote that "For Q1FY27, we have taken closing share price as on 3-Aug-26 (INR 1,398/share)".
